- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.5) — especially after recent spikes — and adjust downward if sentiment drops below 0.3.
- Underestimate prices during low sentiment (sentiment < 0.3) — model tends to be overly conservative, especially in early forecast windows.
- Overshoot after sharp upward moves (e.g., >78) — model often peaks too early and then overcorrects, leading to overprediction in the following 3–5 days.
- Mean-reversion bias: model tends to overreact to recent volatility — forecast often lags true mean by 2–4 days, especially in high-sentiment periods.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are consistently too high in early periods (e.g., 2025-09-17) — model overweights recent momentum, not sentiment or macro trends.
- If sentiment is rising but price is flat or falling, model tends to ignore sentiment and underpredicts upside — adjust forecast upward by 1–2% if sentiment > 0.6 and price < 77.
- If sentiment is falling but price is rising, model often overpredicts — reduce forecast by 1–3% if sentiment < 0.3 and price > 78.
